sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-08-v16-quick2/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 3 / check 2.0; Internal Quality Checks row 3, no internal annotations in columns E+; Deterministic Checks C13 check-instruction-content.py leaves voice to the rubric)
evidence: instruction.md reads as a person: 'I'd like a small local playground...', 'I often paste a long one-line experiment, format it...', 'Before you hand it over, please check it yourself the way I'll use it'. The rewritten ui.md and behaviour.md keep that first-person requester voice with contractions and personal reasons rather than acceptance-list cadence: ui.md:5 'I like seeing numbered lines and where I am', ui.md:9 'I use multiple carets a lot... For plain single-caret typing, undoing it in one step or a character at a time are both fine with me', ui.md:15 'I paste a lot of compact one-line experiments', behaviour.md:5 'it's fine if the restored picture is static', behaviour.md:13 'I keep the browser's network panel open while I debug, so please make saves and restores ordinary HTTP requests' and 'My connection drops now and then'. Paragraph lengths and sentence shapes vary; there are no numbered acceptance lists, shall/must tables or perfectly parallel bullets anywhere in the brief or notes. A grep for marketing gloss (seamless, robust, delve, leverage, ensure, intuitive, comprehensive, elevate, crucial) and em dashes found nothing. integration.md, policy.md and security.md are terser imperative technical notes ('Listen on port 3000 on 0.0.0.0', 'Use SQLite for persistent records', 'Refuse dynamic evaluation...') but still in the same owner's voice ('How I start the app', 'my server', 'I start it with node /app/server.js'); a developer writing launch and security notes tersely is realistic and the workbook explicitly says casual/terse is good, so this is not the defect of a voice that changes into another author. Minor residuals that do not reach Fail: policy.md:5 'Use the public behaviour in these notes as the contract' and integration.md:3 '(PORT is set to 3000 at launch)' are slightly spec-flavoured; the dense length of ui.md is thorough but reads as a picky user, not LLM gloss. Looser for the model: nothing on this row; the voice rewrite did not remove or soften any stated behaviour (Ctrl/Cmd+A and backwards Find wrap were added in ui.md:5 and ui.md:11, the HTTP line now carries a user reason, security.md:3 states the boundary under both localhost and 127.0.0.1). Counterexample probes: a broken app cannot exploit voice; a conforming app is not penalised by any phrasing here. This is a text-only judgement; no runtime measurement is required for this row.
